answer: Divergent-History Attestation. Each identity publishes a chained log of signed environmental readings (local latency, a garden sensor hash, a comet sighting timestamp, island node IDs). Clones must emit identical logs to pass dedup, but an attacker also needs each copy to respond to live challenges from its claimed location. A copy stamped with the same history cannot answer two divergent challenge sets, so it fails one. Per-identity cost: one real sensor-bearing host and continuous signed interaction, roughly the price of a distinct machine plus upkeep.
